slo_title: Find the Fourier series expansion of a function defined in the interval (-l, l).

mcq.q: For \( f(x) \) defined on \( (-L, L) \), the Fourier coefficient \( a_n \) is:

sq.q: \(\text{Explain relationship between Fourier series in } (-\pi,\pi) \text{ and } (-L,L).\)
answer: \(\text{Replace } \pi \text{ by } L \text{ and } x \text{ by } \frac{\pi x}{L} \text{ in } (-\pi,\pi) \text{ formulas}\)
\(\text{Basic forms identical: } f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum (a_n \cos\omega_n x + b_n \sin\omega_n x)\)

sq.q: \(\text{Find Fourier series for } f(x) = x \text{ in } (-L, L). \text{ Is it even or odd?}\)

lq.q: Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=L-|x|\) in \((-L,L)\).
answer: Step Marks Since \(f(x)\) is even, \(b_n=0\) (1) \(a_0=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^L (L-x)dx=L\) (2) \(a_n=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^L (L-x)\cos\frac{n\pi x}{L}dx=\frac{2L}{n^2\pi^2}[1-(-1)^n]\) (5) Thus, \(L-|x|=\frac{L}{2}+\frac{4L}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n-1)^2}\cos\frac{(2n-1)\pi x}{L}\) (4) Put \(x=0\) to get \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n-1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{8}\) (3)
